tailorman_feature_report.md.content:
# Tailorman feature and functionality report

Captured on 31 October 2026 from [Tailorman](https://tailorman.in/dashboard.html), its signed-in business screens, public guided demo, and shipped client code.

The inventory contains **239 feature entries across 37 module groups**. It covers custom tailoring, ready-made boutique sales, customer measurements, production, money collection, stock, staff, reporting, and platform administration.

Open the [complete feature catalog](feature_catalog.md) for every entry and its source evidence. The [CSV inventory](feature_inventory.csv) and [JSON inventory](feature_inventory.json) contain the same entries for planning or import.

## Evidence and coverage

| Evidence | Coverage |
|---|---|
| Authenticated browser | 33 screen and form states in the signed-in admin shop |
| Public browser | 7 states, including login, signup, manual, pricing, tracker error, and two fallback routes |
| Guided demo | 29 static sample screens, explicitly separate from live business records |
| Captured client resources | 134 resources, including 58 first-party JavaScript files and 73 HTML paths |
| REA | All 58 JavaScript files parsed across a main run and a supplementary job-card run |
| Source checks | 443 exact source anchors and line references validated |
| Data and integration references | 150 exported data-helper signatures and five literal custom HTTP API paths |

The signed-in shop had no customers, bills, stock, sales, or sample data. Its account was an admin trial with 17 days remaining. Forms were opened and a bill calculation was exercised without saving. No business records, staff accounts, payments, messages, sample records, or subscription changes were submitted by the investigator. Dismissing the introductory bill tour changed its browser-local completion state.

The feature entries remain code-defined. A related browser screen confirms the layout, form, empty state, or restriction, rather than every behavior described in that entry. Populated details, successful writes, payment settlement, OCR output, customer tracking of a real order, worker access, and super-administrator operations were not tested end to end. Server code and Firestore rules were not supplied.

REA completed syntax parsing without parse failures. The main application graph remains partial and its semantic graph has unresolved relationships. Measurement-template examination was limited by `alias-selections`, although its syntax parsed. The separate [REA findings](rea_findings.md) retain exact Evidence IDs and coverage. These results do not establish complete backend recovery.

## Feature map

| Area | Included functionality |
|---|---|
| Dashboard | Deliveries today, overdue, ready, payment pending, boutique sales, low stock, unassigned cutting and stitching, queues, charts, onboarding checklist, worker wage summary |
| Customers | Name and mobile search, contact details, address, notes, loyalty discount, customer history, measurements, payments, deliveries, alterations, QR card, deletion rules |
| Measurements | Garment-specific numeric, text, boolean, and select fields, family-member label, photos, profile editing and reuse, handwritten-slip scanning with review and undo |
| Garments and packages | 16 default garment types, custom types and measurement templates, sections, drag ordering, service bundles, component quantities, prices, notes, active status |
| Tailoring bills | Auto or manual numbers, customer selection, multiple garment lines, measurements, photos, notes, dates, express surcharge, discount, GST, advance, balance, payment history, edits, voiding, print, PDF, sharing |
| Workshop | Cutter and stitcher assignments, item stages, drag-and-drop production board, urgency and staff filters, refresh, cutting-material deductions, workshop job card |
| Delivery and alterations | Dated delivery groups, capacity indicators, bulk readiness and delivery controls, part-delivery handling, separate alteration lifecycle, outstanding aging and WhatsApp composer |
| Boutique inventory and sales | SKU, size, color, category, supplier, cost, selling price, opening stock, purchase entry, stock adjustments, low-stock alerts, sales cart, split payments, credit sales, receipt and later collections |
| Stitching materials | Fabric and notions stock, units, supplier and costs, stock-in and stock-out, transaction history, low-stock alerts and stock valuation |
| Finance | Accounts daybook, income and expense sources, manual movements, date filters, CSV exports, categorized expenses, tailoring and boutique receivables |
| Staff and wages | Four shop roles, staff account creation, editing, deactivation, password reset, cutting and stitching piece rates, pending payouts, settlements, payout history and voiding |
| Reports | Date presets, tailoring billed value, cash collected, expenses, boutique sales, garment revenue, bill summaries, employee throughput, customer repeat business and CSV export |
| Shop and subscriptions | Shop branding, receipt details, GSTIN, numbering, optional stages, rates, sample data, trial and paid access, expiry, grace, Razorpay renewal and account export |
| Platform administration | Tenant search, state and owner contact, trial extension, activation, suspension, plan limits and flags, pricing, demo controls, cross-shop usage aggregates and CSV export |
| Public and device access | Public tracking link, guided demo, multilingual help and voice narration, tours, manual search, support links, standalone web-app manifest, shortcuts and browser caching |

Detailed module entries are grouped in the [catalog](feature_catalog.md). The [garment schemas](measurement_templates.json) preserve the fields for all 16 defaults.

## Main workflows

### Custom tailoring

Customer selection → garment lines → optional saved measurements, notes and photos → receipt and delivery dates → quantity and rate → express surcharge, discount and GST → advance → save bill → cutting and stitching assignments → production stages → Ready → delivery and remaining collection.

Bill fields include bill number, material-received date, expected delivery date, express flag and surcharge, discount percent, GST percent, advance paid, and order notes. Each garment line has type, quantity, rate, optional measurement ID, notes, and photos. New intake validates dates and customer selection. Auto numbering displays a preview and assigns the actual number when saved.

The browser confirmed this unsaved example:

| Input or result | Value |
|---|---:|
| Garment quantity and rate | 2 × ₹100 |
| Discount | 10% |
| GST | 5% |
| Advance | ₹50 |
| Discounted subtotal | ₹180 |
| Total | ₹189 |
| Balance due | ₹139 |

This confirms the form calculation. It does not establish a saved bill, ledger posting, or receipt. See the [captured preview](evidence/screens/live-new-bill-discount-calculation.json).

### Production and delivery

The detailed sequence has twelve stages:

Material Received → Measurement Taken → Cutting Assigned → Cutting Started → Cutting Completed → Stitching Assigned → Stitching Started → Stitching Completed → Ironing → QC Check → Ready → Delivered.

The production board groups these into broader columns and supports drag advancement, urgency filters, employee filters, manual refresh, and optional 60-second refresh. Cutter and stitcher assignment are per garment line. The admin Work page can show all active items, while worker views use their assignments.

Bill lifecycle values are `pending`, `inProgress`, `ready`, and `delivered`. Item stages, derived urgency, bill lifecycle, and payment balance are separate state concepts. Ironing and QC Check can be disabled in Settings. Whole-bill Ready or Delivered actions can override incomplete item stages after a warning. Therefore mandatory QC is not established by the client.

Delivery schedule groups upcoming work by date over 7, 14, or 30 days. The separate alteration workflow uses Pending → In Progress → Done → Delivered. Both alterations and outstanding aging were blocked by the current trial plan.

### Measurements and scan slip

Customers can have multiple garment profiles and a `forName` label for another wearer. Templates contain sections and number, text, boolean, and select fields. The default types are Suite, Pants, Jeans, Shirt, Shorts, Jubba and Kurtha, Nurse Coat, Blouse, Churidar Kurtha, Churidar, Pavada, Gown, Frock, Lehenga, Alteration, and Dress Materials.

The scan-slip control accepts a photograph, compresses it, and posts it with the selected garment type to `/api/ai/scan-measurement`. High-confidence values can fill the form. Low-confidence values appear as suggestions. Undo restores the prior values, and the tailor still has to save the form. The server's model, recognition accuracy, quotas, and data retention were not observed.

The blank shop prevented opening a customer-linked measurement form through a complete live customer journey without creating a record. The catalog uses the shipped modal handlers and static measurement demo for this flow.

### Boutique counter sale

Create sellable stock → record supplier purchase or stock-in → add products to a sale → set quantities and rates → enter fixed rupee discount and tax → split collection across Cash, UPI, Card, and Bank → complete sale → receipt → collect later against any balance.

Boutique sale states are `paid`, `partial`, and `credit`. An unpaid balance requires a customer name or mobile. Form validation rejects overpayment and a discount greater than the displayed item amount. The code assigns sale numbers, snapshots product details, reduces stock, and writes sale movements and receipts. None of those writes was submitted.

Boutique stock is separate from stitching materials. Boutique tax is a currency amount in this form. Tailoring GST is a percentage. The two billing flows should not be modeled as identical calculations.

### Finance and staff

Accounts combines tailoring receipts, boutique collections, wages, purchases, expenses, and manual movements into a dated daybook. Net Cashflow is income minus expense in the selected period. It is not an accrual profit figure. The manual-entry form accepts Came in or Went out, title, amount, mode, date, party, and notes. Its refund label does not establish an automated product-return flow.

Wages are piece-based for cutting and stitching. Assigned items qualify when they reach the relevant completion stage, and pending calculations use the current configured rate. Admins can select whole item rows to settle, review history, and void an incorrect payout. The live trial blocked the Wages screen, so settlement behavior remains code-defined.

## Roles and access

| Role | Client behavior |
|---|---|
| Admin | Shop setup, staff, customer and order operations, production, financial views, reports, and entitled modules |
| Cashier | Bills, customers, packages, deliveries, boutique counter workflows, and entitled operational sections |
| Cutter | Assigned cutting work, permitted item progression, and worker dashboard information |
| Stitcher | Assigned stitching work, permitted item progression, and worker dashboard information |
| Super administrator | Separate platform guard and console for tenant state, plans, prices, and usage |
| Public customer | Tracking link with tenant and bill identifiers, without the shop sign-in guard |

The [page-guard inventory](platform_page_guards.json) contains 26 explicit client guard declarations. Navigation visibility, page admission, individual controls, and server authorization are separate. Only the signed-in admin role was exercised. Workshop job cards call the general shop auth guard and use the signed-in tenant context.

## Current plans and trial restrictions

These values came from the live plan configuration read through the app on 31 October 2026. They take precedence over older fallback literals in the shipped code. Zero means unlimited in the raw configuration.

| Price or limit | Free | Premium | Business |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| Monthly price | ₹0 | ₹299 | ₹699 |
| Per month on annual cycle | ₹0 | ₹249 | ₹579 |
| Monthly tailoring bills | 150 | 300 | Unlimited |
| Customers | 100 | 200 | Unlimited |
| Seats | 3 | 5 | Unlimited |
| Stitching inventory items | 10 | 20 | Unlimited |
| Boutique items | 10 | 20 | Unlimited |
| Boutique sales per month | 20 | 150 | Unlimited |

The configuration has 15 feature flags. All are enabled for Free and Business in the captured configuration. Premium disables `alterations`, `auditLog`, `boutique`, `expenses`, `outstanding`, and `wages`. The `boutique` flag controls the Boutique & Finance report tab. Counter sales use the separate `boutiqueSales` flag and remain enabled. Advanced reports are enabled for Premium in this live configuration.

That unusual Free/Premium flag ordering is a captured configuration fact. Free-tier runtime access was not tested. A trial uses Premium entitlements, which explains the observed restrictions even though the public page promises every feature during the trial. Five business routes showed a plan-blocking notice: Alterations, Outstanding Payments, Wages, Expenses, and Audit Log. The Boutique & Finance report tab was absent, while Productivity and Customers tabs were visible.

The [live configuration](evidence/live-plan-config.json) and [plan matrix CSV](plan_matrix.csv) contain exact values. The [fallback defaults](platform_plan_defaults.json) are separate. Checkout amounts and subscription activation were not verified through a purchase.

The client supports trial, active, grace, expired, and suspended account states. Paid accounts have a three-day grace period in the inspected state calculation. Renewal offers Premium and Business through Razorpay. Account exports for customers, measurements, and bills are available through an owner export path even after expiry. No self-service Free selection appears in that renewal flow.

## Data and integrations

The client uses Firebase Authentication, Firestore, Storage, and optional App Check headers. Business records are normally accessed under the current tenant. Main entities include customers, measurement profiles, bills and garment lines, item templates, service packages, worker profiles, boutique items, boutique purchases and sales, material stock and movements, payments, wage payouts, expenses, ledger entries, settings, and audit events.

The captured custom HTTP calls are:

| Path | Client purpose |
|---|---|
| `POST /api/ai/scan-measurement` | Read a photographed measurement slip |
| `POST /api/employees/set-password` | Set an existing staff password |
| `POST /api/billing/order` | Create a subscription checkout order |
| `POST /api/billing/verify` | Submit Razorpay payment verification values |
| `POST /api/account/export` | Export owner account data as CSV |

These five references are not a complete API specification. Most business data operations call Firebase directly. The [data-helper signatures](data_helpers.csv), [collection references](data_collection_references.json), and [client HTTP references](client_api_calls.csv) retain the source locations.

WhatsApp controls open prefilled composer links. They do not prove message dispatch or delivery. Public tracking performs one document read when the page opens. The module has no periodic refresh or realtime listener, so a customer may need to reload to see a later stage.

The web manifest declares standalone installation and shortcuts. The service worker caches shell resources, images, scripts, and voice clips. Firestore has local persistence behavior. These declarations do not prove that all writes, payments, or scans work offline.

## Material findings and reconstruction cautions

These findings identify behavior that matters when using the inventory to rebuild or improve the product. Unless browser evidence is named, they are static findings with untested write paths.

1. **Trial access differs from the public promise.** Live Premium flags block six capabilities, and five protected routes showed plan notices. Use the captured configuration rather than the claim that every feature is unlocked.
2. **Positive opening stock for stitching materials appears to double.** The creation handler stores the entered stock and then records the same quantity as stock-in. For an entered 10, the inspected path implies 20. No item was saved to test this. Boutique opening stock uses a different path.
3. **Zero boutique sale rates can disagree with the preview.** The form uses zero, while the data helper substitutes the product selling price when the rate is zero or below. Persisted totals and balance need a live check.
4. **Package headline price is not applied to bill lines.** The picker displays the package price but adds component quantities and rates. A reconstruction needs an explicit decision about bundle pricing.
5. **Historical bills refer to current measurement profiles.** They retain a measurement ID rather than an independent measurement snapshot in the inspected path. Editing or deleting that profile can change what an older bill displays.
6. **QC is optional.** Settings can disable it, and whole-bill actions can override unfinished stages after warning. The mandatory-QC marketing statement is too broad.
7. **Several totals use capped input.** Customer search scans 500 customers, bill substring search scans 500 bills, customer history summarizes 100 bills, Outstanding reads 300, and several financial views cap sales or ledger rows at 500. Reports warns on its relevant cap. Counts outside those windows remain unknown.
8. **Some related writes are separate.** Bill advance, wage ledger, purchase expense, alteration ledger, and cutting-stock work include sequential operations rather than one shared transaction. Failure recovery was not exercised. Multi-line boutique sale transaction ordering and repeated product IDs also need a populated checkout check.
9. **Display masking does not cover every output path.** Worker bill detail hides money on screen, but the inspected Print, PDF, and Share templates include financial values without the same display guard. No worker account or server permission boundary was tested.
10. **Some links and settings do not complete the implied action.** Audit entity links all target the bill page. Already-active tenant plan selectors have no persistence action in the inspected console. Those should not be treated as implemented updates merely because a control exists.
11. **Two measurement routes fall back to the landing page.** Both `/measurement.html` and `/measurement-qr.html` displayed the product homepage. The working measurement modal and generated QR-card content are separate features. A 200 response does not establish a working standalone route.
12. **The public tracker has a fixed stage presentation.** It keeps Ironing and QC in its seven-step display even if the shop skips those stages, and reads once at load.

The source-level [core findings](core_findings.md), [operations findings](operations_findings.md), and [platform findings](platform_findings.md) contain further bounded details, including source references. Their scope statements describe each static subtask. This report adds the parent investigation's authenticated browser evidence and current configuration.

## Deliverables and validation

- [Complete catalog](feature_catalog.md), [CSV](feature_inventory.csv), and [JSON](feature_inventory.json).
- [Browser observation index](browser_observations.csv) with 69 recorded states, separated by evidence type.
- [Captured HTML paths](routes.csv), including explicit landing-page fallbacks.
- [Live plan matrix](plan_matrix.csv) and [garment measurement schemas](measurement_templates.json).
- [REA method and Evidence IDs](rea_findings.md), [machine coverage summary](evidence/rea-summary.json), and [asset hashes](evidence/asset-provenance.json).
- [Validation result](validation.json) and [inventory totals](inventory_summary.json).

`python3 research_tailorman/build_inventory.py` regenerates the catalog and machine-readable indexes, checks every feature anchor and line, verifies all captured-resource hashes, and checks the recorded unsaved bill result. It does not run the target application or submit business actions.

## Workflow model

The detailed production sequence has 12 stages: Material Received → Measurement Taken → Cutting Assigned → Cutting Started → Cutting Completed → Stitching Assigned → Stitching Started → Stitching Completed → Ironing → QC Check → Ready → Delivered. Bill lifecycle values include pending, inProgress, ready, and delivered. Derived urgency labels are separate from these stored lifecycle values. Ironing and QC Check can be disabled.

Customer selection → garment lines → optional measurements/photos → pricing, advance, discount, GST → bill creation → assignment and production → Ready → optional delivery collection → Delivered. Whole-bill status actions can override incomplete stages after a warning. Undo changes workflow state while retaining recorded money.

## Material differences and limits

### Search and summaries are bounded

Customer search scans the first 500 customers, bill substring search the latest 500 bills, and the customer profile summarizes its newest 100 bills. These are retrieval limits, not whole-shop completeness guarantees.

operations_findings.md.content:
# Tailorman operations feature findings

This source review records 78 code-defined feature entries across ten modules in [operations_features.json](operations_features.json). Every entry contains an exact captured-source anchor and line number. The review used the shipped JavaScript and corresponding HTML captured from Tailorman. It did not execute authenticated business actions, create staff, record purchases, collect payments, or settle wages. The parent investigation supplies browser corroboration and REA Evidence identities separately.

## Boutique inventory and sales

Boutique stock has its own `boutiqueInventory` collection, distinct from stitching materials. Each sellable item stores category, unit, SKU, size, color, supplier, notes, stock, alert threshold, cost, and selling price. The UI has search and filters, cost and retail valuation, low-stock alerts, stock adjustments, transaction history, purchase entry, and recent purchases. Purchases store a supplier and invoice, update stock and last cost, and post an expense to the ledger.

Sales accept any number of product lines, editable quantities and prices, fixed discount and tax amounts, customer contact, and notes. Payments can be split across cash, UPI, card, and bank, or omitted for a full-credit sale. A remaining balance requires at least a customer name or mobile. The client rejects overpayment and a discount larger than the displayed item total. Sale statuses are `paid`, `partial`, and `credit`.

The data layer reserves sale numbers as `SYY-00001`, snapshots product fields into the sale, reduces stock, writes item movements, and posts initial receipts to Accounts within the transaction. Sale detail prints a receipt and supports later split collections against the balance. History has date, status, payment-mode, and text filters. See [sales.js](evidence/assets/js/sales.js), [sale.js](evidence/assets/js/sale.js), [sales-history.js](evidence/assets/js/sales-history.js), [boutique-inventory.js](evidence/assets/js/boutique-inventory.js), and [db.js](evidence/assets/js/db.js).

## Materials and finance

Stitching materials support ten categories and thirteen stock units. The master includes supplier, cost, notes, stock, and low-stock threshold. Users can restock, issue materials, view transaction history, filter inventory, and inspect valuation. Stock-out rejects an issue beyond available quantity. Stock-in with a cost also records a material-purchase expense. The data helper accepts an optional bill ID, although the inventory adjustment form does not expose that link.

Accounts is a dated cash daybook. Income minus expense is labeled Net Cashflow. It is not an accrual profit statement. Source groups distinguish tailoring payments, boutique sales, purchases, wages, expenses, and manual entries. Admins can add other money movements, such as drawings, capital, loans, and refunds, using a title, positive amount, type, mode, date, party, and notes. This generic manual-entry feature does not establish a product-return or automated refund workflow. Only manual entries are deleted directly from this page. CSV export uses the current loaded date range. See [accounts.js](evidence/assets/js/accounts.js).

Expenses support entry, edit, delete, date filtering, category filtering, totals, highest category, and average expense. Each expense synchronizes a linked ledger entry. Categories are Rent, Electricity, Staff Salary, Material Purchase, Equipment, Maintenance, Marketing, Transport, and Miscellaneous. See [expenses.js](evidence/assets/js/expenses.js).

Outstanding tailoring bills are separate from boutique receivables. They include delivered bills that still have a balance. Aging uses expected delivery date, with Not Yet Due, 1-7, 8-30, and 31-plus-day groups. The WhatsApp link opens a prefilled composer and always prepends `91` to the stored digits. It does not prove that a message was sent. See [outstanding.js](evidence/assets/js/outstanding.js).

## Reports

Reports use common date presets and custom dates across Overview, Bills, Boutique & Finance, Productivity, and Customers. Plan checks remove unsupported tabs. Overview distinguishes value billed during the period from cash collected during the period. The latter comes from income ledger entries and includes money received against older bills. Bill-level paid totals remain based on bills created in the selected period.

Tailoring revenue changes between daily and monthly SVG charts depending on range length. Garment revenue ranks the top eight item types using quantity times rate. Productivity counts timeline events by actor name and stage. The events are taken from bills created in the range, so this is not a pure completion-date productivity report. Customer reports group by mobile, falling back to name, and classify two or more bills in the selected period as repeat business. Their retention percentage is a period repeat-order ratio, not lifetime cohort retention. Exports follow the active report tab. See [reports.js](evidence/assets/js/reports.js).

## Staff and wages

Admins can create email/password staff accounts, assign one of admin/cashier/cutter/stitcher, change name and role, deactivate a profile, and set a new password through `/api/employees/set-password`. Email is read-only after creation. Password creation and reset require at least six characters. Accounts are created through a secondary Firebase app so the admin stays signed in. Profile save and password change have distinct success/failure handling. Active seats are counted before creating new staff; the check allows creation if counting fails. See [employees.js](evidence/assets/js/employees.js).

Wages use separate current master rates for cutting and stitching. Assigned items qualify once their current stage reaches Cutting Completed or Stitching Completed. The code excludes already-paid bill/item/role keys and multiplies quantities by the current rate. Admins can settle a selected subset of whole item rows, view payment history, and void a mistaken settlement. Voiding deletes payment and linked ledger entry together, returning those items to pending on reload. Recording a wage payment stores the wage document before posting its cash expense. See [wages.js](evidence/assets/js/wages.js) and [db.js](evidence/assets/js/db.js).

Workers have a dashboard wage panel with today, total pending, paid in the last 30 days, item details, last payout, and payout history. The 30-day figure filters only the latest 30 returned payout records. See [dashboard.js](evidence/assets/js/dashboard.js).

Audit history is an admin viewer with exact-action filters, actor, time, details, and an entity link. The client writes events for bills, stages, payments, expenses, wages, sales, purchases, customer deletion, staff changes, and settings. Many audit writes swallow failures. Browser code alone does not prove server-enforced immutability or complete audit capture. See [audit-log.js](evidence/assets/js/audit-log.js).

## Material findings and limits

1. Positive material opening stock appears to double in the inspected creation path. `inventory.js` line 318 sets `data.stockQty` to the entered quantity, and line 321 passes the same quantity to `recordStockIn`. `saveInventoryItem` stores the payload unchanged. `recordStockIn` then adds the quantity to the stored value. For an entered 10, this code path implies 20. This was not executed on a live item.
2. A zero sale rate can disagree with the form preview. `sales.js` multiplies the entered rate directly. `db.js` line 2316 replaces a rate at zero or below with the product selling price. That may change the stored total and balance from the values validated by the form. The mismatch is static evidence, not a submitted-sale result.
3. Multi-line boutique sales need a live check. `createBoutiqueSale` performs a product read and then writes inside each loop iteration, and the next iteration reads again. Duplicate item IDs are not combined before those operations. This review records the ordering and unresolved execution behavior without asserting a successful multi-line sale.
4. The audit viewer routes every entity ID to `bill.html`, including wage, expense, staff, and sale events. The generic link at `audit-log.js` line 45 does not dispatch by entity type.
5. Not all cross-record writes share one transaction. Boutique purchases, material purchases, wages, and expenses post their ledger entries after committing their source mutation. The actual failure recovery and server rules remain unverified. Expense ledger cleanup ignores errors in `removeAccountEntry`.
6. Several totals have bounded input. Sales history reads 500, today's sale KPIs 200, Accounts 500 ledger rows and 500 sales, Expenses 200, Outstanding 300, and pending wages 500 bills plus 2000 payments. Reports explicitly warns when its 500-row boutique or ledger cap is reached. These caps do not establish the number of records in the live shop.
7. Status or payment-mode filters apply to a sale's aggregate mode. Split sales use `mixed`, while the inspected history select offers cash, UPI, card, and bank. A cash component within a mixed sale does not match the cash filter.

## Source validation

`python3 research_tailorman/build_operations_inventory.py` regenerates the JSON and asserts that every source anchor exists before deriving its line. All 78 entries remain code-defined, with explicit untested behavior. Client-side role checks and plan gates are described as observed code. This review does not infer Firestore rules or Cloud Function authorization from them.

platform_findings.md.content:
# Tailorman platform and public-flow findings

This pass extracted 60 code-defined entries across 12 module sections. It covers identity, shop onboarding, tenant context, plans, subscription billing, settings, platform administration, customer tracking, workshop job cards, help, public entry points and browser caching. The parent investigation supplies browser observations and actual REA Evidence IDs separately.

The inventory is [platform_features.json](platform_features.json). Each entry includes exact source text and a line number. [build_platform_features.py](build_platform_features.py) regenerates and checks those anchors without executing target JavaScript. [platform_plan_defaults.json](platform_plan_defaults.json) records fallback plan literals. [platform_page_guards.json](platform_page_guards.json) records 26 client page guards.

## Identity and tenant setup

The app supports Google popup sign-in and email/password sign-in through Firebase Authentication. Google users can create a shop directly. Email-signup users supply shop name, full name, email, optional dial code and phone, password and confirmation. Client validation requires eight password characters, matching passwords, and 6 to 15 phone digits when a phone is entered. Verification email must precede tenant provisioning. The verify panel checks user verification every four seconds, allows manual continuation, supports a local 60-second resend cooldown, and can discard an unverified signup to use another email.

Provisioning writes a tenant, a userTenants mapping, an active admin profile and shop settings, then seeds default garment types. The mapping currently resolves one tenant per user. Phone onboarding can be completed or skipped. Presence of ownerPhone marks onboarding complete, including an empty value. These are client paths. No signup or verification email was submitted by this pass.

The four shop roles are admin, cashier, cutter and stitcher. A separate superAdmins document determines platform access. Client page guards and role-aware navigation are explicit. A change to the server profile can sign out an inactive user or reload a changed role. Firestore and Storage rules were not supplied, so the inventory does not claim tested backend authorization.

Sources include [auth.js](evidence/assets/js/auth.js), [login.js](evidence/assets/js/login.js), [signup.js](evidence/assets/js/signup.js), [onboarding.js](evidence/assets/js/onboarding.js) and [tenant.js](evidence/assets/js/tenant.js).

## Plans use live overrides and older fallback defaults

The client reads superAdminSettings/plans and merges saved fields with fallback defaults. Six plan limits and 15 feature flags exist. Zero means unlimited.

These are the shipped defaults, not the current commercial offer:

| Limit or price | Free | Premium | Business |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| Monthly bills | 30 | Unlimited | Unlimited |
| Customers | 50 | Unlimited | Unlimited |
| Seats | 1 | 4 | Unlimited |
| Stitching inventory items | 10 | Unlimited | Unlimited |
| Boutique items | 10 | Unlimited | Unlimited |
| Boutique sales per month | 20 | Unlimited | Unlimited |
| Monthly price | ₹0 | ₹599 | ₹1299 |
| Annual monthly equivalent | ₹0 | ₹499 | ₹1099 |

Free defaults enable stitching inventory and boutique sales, with limits. Premium defaults enable all flags except advanced reports, expenses and audit log. Business defaults enable all 15 flags. The public-home browser observation captured by the parent shows different live commercial prices and limits. Use those runtime values for the actual offer. The code defaults remain useful only for fallback behavior.

The public landing module updates visible pricing cards and the FAQ price span from live configuration. Static FAQ limits, structured metadata and some renewal highlights still contain older defaults. This explains why raw HTML or marketing strings can disagree with the rendered plan cards.

Sources: [tenant.js](evidence/assets/js/tenant.js), [landing.js](evidence/assets/js/landing.js), [root HTML](evidence/pages/root.html), [public-home observation](evidence/screens/public-home.json).

## Subscription behavior

New shops receive a trial length from live pricing.trialDays, falling back to 30. Trials use Premium entitlements and limits. They do not automatically use Business entitlements, despite public copy describing access to every feature. The precise trial experience therefore depends on the saved Premium feature flags.

The state calculator supports trial, active, grace, expired and suspended. Trials have no grace. Paid periods have three grace days. An active tenant without paidUntil does not expire according to the client calculation. The client synchronizes a clock from an origin Date header when possible, checks local expiry each minute, refreshes tenant state when returning to the tab, and probes for account lock after permission denial. A lock attempts to terminate Firestore and clear IndexedDB before redirect, with a three-second cap. A static cache-clearing attempt does not establish a guaranteed wipe.

The owner renewal page offers Premium and Business, monthly or annual, using live prices. It has no self-service Free selection in the inspected flow. Staff see owner-directed renewal wording. Suspension hides the payment choices because payment does not lift a platform suspension.

Checkout creates an order at POST /api/billing/order, opens Razorpay, and verifies the payment response at POST /api/billing/verify. Requests carry Firebase Authentication and optional App Check headers. Account CSV exports for customers, measurements and bills use POST /api/account/export and are offered to owners after expiry or suspension. No checkout, export or subscription change was performed. Server price computation, signature checks, webhook behavior and authorization remain outside captured client evidence.

Sources: [auth.js](evidence/assets/js/auth.js), [ui.js](evidence/assets/js/ui.js), [trial-expired.js](evidence/assets/js/trial-expired.js), [billing.js](evidence/assets/js/billing.js).

## Shop configuration

Admin settings cover shop name, tagline, address, phone, email and GSTIN, default cutting and stitching rates, auto or manual bill numbers, prefix and counter reset. Counter reset warns before reusing issued numbers and requires an explicit override to move backwards.

The workflow settings can omit Ironing and QC Check from the shop's active stages. This is meaningful configuration: the public statement that no order can reach Ready without QC is too broad for the inspected implementation.

The sample-data action writes five customers, three measurement profiles, six bills and three expenses into the current tenant. Records carry a sample flag and duplicate sample loading is skipped. Cleanup removes flagged customer, bill and expense records, plus every measurement under a flagged sample customer. Consequently, a new unflagged measurement later added to a sample customer would also be removed during cleanup. No sample loading or cleanup was run.

Sources: [settings.js](evidence/assets/js/settings.js), [db.js](evidence/assets/js/db.js), [sample-data.js](evidence/assets/js/sample-data.js).

## Platform administration

The super-administrator console includes tenant search, owner contact details, effective states, plan and cycle display, 30-day trial extension, manual activation, suspension and reactivation. It edits all tier limits and feature flags plus currency, prices and trial length. A WhatsApp welcome control opens a prefilled composer; it does not send a message automatically.

A separate usage console progressively aggregates customers, bills, billed amount, collected amount and outstanding per tenant, ranks shops by billed amount, supports search and refresh, and exports visible rows as CSV. Missing composite indexes can cause an unfiltered aggregate fallback including soft-deleted rows. The UI marks such results approximate. KPI totals cover all successful shop rows rather than the current search subset.

Two code concerns are bounded to the inspected console:

- On an already active tenant, the visible plan and cycle selectors have no change handler or Save action. They are read only by the Activate handler for non-active tenants. An imported setTenantPlan helper is unused in this module. Do not assume changing either selector persists a change.
- The demo-enable handler writes a legacy pro plan. The inspected plan lookup recognizes Free, Premium and Business and falls back to Free configuration for an unknown key. This needs runtime verification before claiming the demo has the intended entitlements. Shipped credential values are omitted from authored findings.

Sources: [super-admin.js](evidence/assets/js/super-admin.js), [super-admin-usage.js](evidence/assets/js/super-admin-usage.js), [tenant.js](evidence/assets/js/tenant.js).

## Public tracker and authenticated workshop job card

The public tracker accepts tid and id and reads the indicated bill without calling the shop auth guard. It displays bill number, customer name, delivery date, balance, status, item type, quantity, description and shop name. Missing identifiers, unavailable documents or failed reads show Order not found. It maps detailed stages to Received, Cutting, Stitching, Ironing, QC, Ready and Delivered, using the least-advanced item as the progress bottleneck with a bill-level Ready or Delivered floor.

The tracker uses one getDoc at page load, with no realtime listener or periodic refresh in the inspected module. It always renders the seven macro stages and does not load the shop's skipped-stage settings. Therefore 'live' tracking means the server value when the page loads, not proved automatic updates while the customer keeps the page open. The tracker reads a full bill document, so its limited display fields are not proof of a restricted public server response. Anonymous read permissions and real order contents were not tested by this static pass.

The workshop job card requires authentication and accepts any shop role through requireAuth with no role list. It parses the URL tenant ID but does not use it; getBill reads the signed-in tenant context. It shows customer contact details, due date, notes, express status, garment instructions, assigned workers, measurements, material photos, inspiration images and stage progress. The inspected page has no payment totals and no stage-advance actions. Measurements come from current linked customer profiles rather than an independent historical measurement snapshot.

Captured measurement.html and measurement-qr.html contain the public landing page, even though the response status is 200. Those captures do not establish working measurement routes. The parent is checking the actual QR flows and browser behavior separately.

Sources: [bill-track.js](evidence/assets/js/bill-track.js), [job-card.js](evidence/assets/js/job-card.js), [bill-track HTML](evidence/pages/bill-track.html), [measurement HTML](evidence/pages/measurement.html), [measurement QR HTML](evidence/pages/measurement-qr.html).

## Help and device behavior

The working-page help panel has Malayalam, Hindi, Tamil, Telugu and Kannada choices, stored locally. It requests page-specific JSON tips, provides fallback text, and loads voice guidance lazily. It includes a WhatsApp support composer with the current page identifier. Voice narration and guided tours are covered by the core-flow inventory.

The public manual has sidebar text filtering and section highlighting. Public entry points include product pages, academy guides, the guided demo, signup, pricing, support channels, terms and privacy. Documentation and policy statements remain claims unless separately supported by shipped handlers or runtime evidence.

The web manifest declares standalone installation and New Bill, Customers and Production shortcuts. The service worker precaches common shell resources, caches images and voice clips, revalidates script and style assets, and uses network-first HTML with cached fallback. Firestore uses persistent multiple-tab local caching with memory fallback. None of those declarations proves every transaction or form works offline. No native store app or installation was tested.

Sources: [help.js](evidence/assets/js/help.js), [manual HTML](evidence/pages/manual.html), [manifest](evidence/pages/manifest.json), [service worker](evidence/assets/sw.js), [firebase.js](evidence/assets/js/firebase.js).

## Verification boundary

All 60 entries have checked source anchors and line numbers. No target JavaScript was executed by this pass. No browser actions, network requests, messages, account creation, billing operations, exports or business-record mutations were performed by this subtask. The parent investigation combines these static findings with its browser observations and REA results. Entries should remain code-defined even when a related empty screen or form has been observed.

# REA findings and evidence boundary

The installed [reverse-engineer-anything skill](/Users/nishanth/.agents/skills/reverse-engineer-anything/SKILL.md) guided this investigation. It was already installed from the Nool Tech task. No reinstall was needed.

The skill supplies instructions. No REA MCP connection was available in this session. The existing `rea-agents` 6.8.0 CLI was used through the skill's documented JavaScript fallback. Browser inspection and asset acquisition used the shared T3 browser. No separate browser runtime was launched by REA.

## Acquisition

First-party HTML, scripts, the manifest, English help text, and the voice manifest were fetched through the page's browser context. The resource list was expanded from actual script imports, navigation links, referenced route strings, and the public demo's declared flow. Firebase SDK and other external vendor modules were not copied into the static target. Backend Cloud Functions, Firestore rules, and server-only routes were unavailable.

There are 134 retained resources, including 58 first-party JavaScript files. Browser text was serialized in acquisition JSON, then written as exact UTF-8 bytes. The SHA-256 of each retained file matches the digest computed over the browser response text. Initial responses were checked with a later digest read and matched. This establishes retained decoded-text identity, not the original compressed wire bytes or a deployment signature.

[Asset provenance](evidence/asset-provenance.json) retains URL, response status, local path, byte length, and digest. The acquisition JSON files preserve the response text. [unpack_evidence.py](unpack_evidence.py) reproduces the extracted files and checks hashes.

## REA runs

The main run analyzed the first 57 captured JavaScript files:

```text
rea analyze-javascript-application <absolute evidence/assets directory>
  --detail summary --evidence_output <absolute evidence/rea-evidence.json> --json
```

Parent Evidence ID: `ev_b52d8793fef92ae8e00b4ebe22800fac47c0b7eeaaf5a673b481d4c11b46ca4e`.

Summary Evidence ID: `ev_2c7215a9a20af9561632e7de0046c7a92ce587ceae0734560d6b2b71fb71b49b`.

The run parsed 57 files and 104,905 AST nodes with no parse failures. Syntax coverage was complete for all 57. Examination was complete for 56 and limited for `js/measurement-templates.js` by the `alias-selections` semantic limit. The application graph was partial, and semantic graph coverage was unknown. It retained 25,623 semantic unknowns. Full syntax coverage does not resolve those dynamic relationships.

The job-card module was discovered later through a template-string link. It was analyzed once with an exact source selection:

```text
rea analyze-javascript-application <absolute evidence/assets directory>
  --source-path js/job-card.js --detail summary
  --evidence_output <absolute evidence/rea-job-card-evidence.json> --json
```

Parent Evidence ID: `ev_414b3f2b7be166d33f0f4132f525ec2921deea55225fc46dc88e2f5df68423e4`.

That run parsed the selected 9,106-byte module without parse failures. Its inventory included the expanded 58-file tree. It did not reanalyze the other 57 sources. The two artifact-root digests differ because the job-card file was added between runs.

Combined source syntax coverage is 58 parsed files, 58 syntax-complete files, and zero parse failures. Combined examination is 57 complete and one limited. Target bootstrap code was not executed by REA. There were no provider timeouts in these Tailorman runs.

The automatic route inventory from the first-party JavaScript target did not enumerate the HTML screen map. The [73 captured HTML paths](routes.csv) were independently derived from acquired resources and browser navigation. They are not a complete server-route denominator. Five captured paths returned the landing page rather than the named application screen.

| Question | Evidence | Result and limit |
|---|---|---|
| What can the business app do? | Captured handlers, HTML, 33 authenticated states, 29 static demo states, REA parents above | 239 source-anchored feature entries. Successful writes remain untested. |
| What does the current trial allow? | Live plan configuration and five route restrictions | Premium trial flags observed. Free flags were read but Free runtime was not tested. |
| How do charges calculate? | New Bill handlers and unsaved browser preview | ₹200 at 10% discount plus 5% GST gives ₹189, then ₹50 advance leaves ₹139. No saved bill or ledger validation. |
| What are the states and entities? | Data helpers, stage constants, field templates, role guards | Client model recovered. Server constraints, full schema, and cross-record atomicity are unverified. |
| Which custom APIs exist? | Five literal HTTP paths and their callers | Five client references, not a complete API specification or evidence of successful requests. |
| Is all functionality exercised? | Empty live shop, plan restrictions, no worker or platform-admin session | No. Populated detail, checkout, scan results, worker permissions, and platform mutations remain code-defined. |
