tailormate_feature_report.md.content:
# TailorMate feature and functionality report

Captured on 31 October 2026 from [TailorMate Web](https://web.tailormateapp.com/), its signed-in screens, and its shipped Next.js client.

The inventory contains **209 feature entries across 36 module groups**. It covers stitching orders, material and readymade sales, customer measurements, tasks, workshop scheduling, stores, stock, workers, payments, reporting, and shop configuration.

The [complete feature catalog](feature_catalog.md) contains every entry with exact source evidence and verification gaps. The [CSV](feature_inventory.csv) and [JSON](feature_inventory.json) contain the same entries for planning or import.

## Evidence and coverage

| Evidence | Coverage |
|---|---|
| Authenticated browser | 71 screen and form states |
| Public browser | Login and unsubmitted registration |
| Client resources | 213 resources, including 163 JavaScript files and 50 HTML paths |
| Compiled client pages | 45 page patterns, including dynamic order and task detail |
| REA | 73 selected application scripts examined across two runs, with zero parse failures |
| Source validation | 472 exact feature anchors and offsets checked against retained scripts |
| HTTP references | 285 literal call sites, representing 119 distinct method/path pairs |

The signed-in shop had no customers, orders, material stock, readymade stock, or worker records. Standard roles, inventory types, sizes, task definitions, bill terms, add-ons, and gallery folders were available. The investigator opened forms and changed local preview controls without saving. No business records, payments, uploads, messages, settings, backup schedules, or worker accounts were submitted.

Every catalog entry remains code-defined. Related browser evidence confirms a visible screen, form, control, empty state, or unsaved preview. It does not establish every behavior in that entry. Customer-linked garment entry, populated order details, worker payouts, generated documents, uploads, delivery notifications, and backup execution were not tested end to end.

The order-detail and task-detail bundles were acquired from literal template URL requests. Those requests discovered shipped code without using a valid business-record ID. They do not establish a successful record load or access to another shop's data.

REA examined application pages and shared business helpers. Ninety captured scripts were outside its selected scope. Its application and semantic graphs remain partial, with resource limits and unresolved relationships. [REA findings](rea_findings.md) retain the exact Evidence IDs and coverage. Backend source, database schema, authorization rules, and the mobile application were outside this capture.

## Feature map

| Area | Included functionality |
|---|---|
| Customers | Search, name, mobile, email, birth date, gender, height, weight, address, GSTIN, face and body photographs, profile editing and deactivation |
| Measurements | Gender-specific body templates, illustrated fields, garment measurement profiles, names and notes, saved-set reuse, copy and edit, body-to-garment mapping, order measurement data |
| Stitching orders | Customer selection, garment and service type, nickname, quantity, urgency, delivery and function dates, trials, sales staff, instructions, video link, charges, add-ons, cloth and pattern photos |
| Material and readymade sales | Stock pickers, quantity and selling-price entry, stock-limit checks, line additions, edits and deactivation through the shared order workflow |
| Order operations | Active, Past Due, Upcoming, Completed, Urgent and Delivered queues, list period, search, advanced filters, dates, status changes, item actions and financial overview |
| Documents and collection | Dated receipts, payment methods, payment editing and removal, discounts, balance, bills, payment advice, item and whole-order print files, QR outputs and WhatsApp composers |
| Tasks and calendar | Task planning, staff allocation, piece rates, expected dates, start and finish events, comments, reset, operational task queues, four-month workload view and color ranges |
| Gallery | Folders, image upload, favorites, image removal and carousel inspection |
| Stock and purchases | Separate material and readymade masters, SKU, type, unit or sizes, prices, stock, supplier, images, purchase entry and editing, purchase filters and CSV |
| Workforce | Mobile-based users, shop-role assignments, permission roles, garment rates, worker dues, selected-row payouts, payout reports, dress and task assignment reports |
| Administration | Task definitions, custom garments, measurement icons and names, stitching-feature groups, expense heads, bill terms, stitch types and priced add-ons |
| Stores and configuration | Store directory, two-step setup, main-shop copying, address and map location, branding photos, services, units, GST, numbering, notifications, templates and backup schedule |
| Dashboard and reports | Period and location filters, sales and payments, operational counts, sales-type and prediction charts, insights, monthly series, grouped sales, receipts, dues, bills and Excel requests |
| Identity and support | Mobile OTP sign-in, registration and consent, first-store setup, shop access, permission-aware navigation, theme, fullscreen, FAQs and contact links |

The [catalog](feature_catalog.md) expands this map into the 209 individual entries.

## Main workflows

### Customer and measurement record

Add customer → enter contact and personal details → optionally add body measurements and photographs → save customer → add named garment measurement profiles → reuse or copy a profile in a stitching order.

The live customer form exposed name, country dial code and mobile, email, birth date, Male/Female selection, height, weight, address, customer GSTIN, face image, body image, and Add body measurement. The body-measurement modal opened without a saved customer. In this new-account session it displayed notes without populated dimension rows, so a complete live measurement-template interaction was not established.

Body and garment definitions come from server responses. The code supports illustrated measurement fields and merges existing values by measurement ID. The customer garment wizard first selects a gender-specific garment and then accepts a named set of values. The inspected measurement editors label inches and serialize `measurement_unit: IN`. A unit-conversion workflow is not established by those handlers, even though Settings offers Cms and Inch.

In order entry, saved measurement sets are filtered to the garment. A selected set can be viewed read-only, or copied and edited with its original profile identifiers cleared. Order items include the chosen measurement values and profile references. The stock-sale branches do not use this garment-measurement flow.

### Stitching order

Choose New Stitching → select customer → select garment → enter garment details → save → inspect order → assign staff and tasks → record progress and collection → produce documents and complete the order workflow.

The browser confirmed the category picker and stitching stepper. The empty customer register prevented progressing through a complete order without creating a customer.

The garment editor supports:

- Garment nickname, stitch type, quantity and default garment price.
- Up to two sales staff per garment.
- Visual stitching options, including illustrated choices.
- Measurement-dress-given and urgent flags.
- Base charge and repeated priced add-ons.
- Required delivery date and 48 half-hour time choices, with 17:00 as the new-item default.
- Optional function date and trial date/time rows.
- Special instructions and a video-link string.
- Cloth photographs with length, comments and per-piece item number, plus separate pattern photographs.

The client offers more trial rows than it serializes. Its save payload contains only the first three as `trial_date`, `trial_date2`, and `trial_date3`. This is recorded as an implementation gap rather than reproduced as a recommended requirement.

### Material or readymade sale

Choose the sale category → select customer → choose stocked items → enter quantities and selling prices → save through the shared order service → collect and produce order documents.

Material sales have a two-step customer/material stepper. Readymade sales have a customer/readymade stepper. Both categories were opened in the browser. Customer selection is still required to proceed in this session.

The picker shows stock, identifying fields and images. Readymades also show size. Search matches name, type and SKU. The client requires at least one positive quantity, rejects a quantity above displayed stock, and rejects an empty, nonnumeric or negative price for a selected line. Existing saved lines set to zero are submitted as inactive updates.

New stitching orders and both stock-sale categories share `/saveneworder`; edits use `/updateorder`. That shared endpoint does not establish shared backend stock transactions or identical pricing rules.

### Order control, collection and documents

The order overview combines garments, material lines and readymade lines. It exposes customer contact, dates, order number, server-provided statuses, garment details, measurements, photographs and permission-controlled money sections.

The client computes its displayed order amount from garment price fields and the stock lines' `total_price` values. Balance subtracts recorded receipts and discount. The inspected view does not recover backend quantity expansion or tax calculation, so this report does not assign it another product's GST formula.

Receive Payment has amount, date and payment method. Past receipts can be inspected, edited or deactivated. Discount uses a separate `payment_type: 2` record; ordinary receipts use type 1. The inspected payment schemas do not establish positive-number or overpayment limits.

Bills and payment advice come from `/getorderinvoice`. Separate print services produce garment, whole-order and QR files. The UI can display, download, print or share returned URLs. WhatsApp actions open composers; no message dispatch or delivery was tested.

`Finish Order` is a separate intake-finalization request when the detail URL has a `from` value. It should not be confused with changing an order's lifecycle status.

### Workshop tasks and workload

Define task types and days → plan garment tasks backwards from delivery → assign staff → start the first unfinished task → finish with comments → review task progress and worker earnings.

Task workflow values in the client are 1 Not Started, 2 In Progress and 3 Completed. Active, Delayed, Due Today, Due Tomorrow and Completed are operational task queues. On Time and Delayed badges are derived presentation states rather than additional workflow IDs.

Starting records actor and time. Finishing records actor, end time and comments. Canceling a start resets the task to Not Started with a zero-date start sentinel. Task planning locks some controls after work has started.

The work calendar covers the current month and the next three months, with daily delivery counts, monthly totals, average orders per day, busiest day and maximum daily count. Days with orders can open filtered order search. A settings modal edits workload ranges and colors. Numeric ordering, overlap and gaps are not validated by the captured range schema.

### Stock and purchasing

Materials and readymades have separate records. Both include name, type, SKU, current stock, selling price, purchase price, supplier and two image slots. Materials use a unit; readymades use sizes. The browser confirmed these forms without saving.

Current stock is editable in the item form. Later purchases use Add Stock with quantity, purchase unit price and supplier. Purchase editing retains the purchase ID. The date is displayed as text in that dialog.

The Purchases report defaults to 180 days. It can filter both categories or one, search SKU, group by date or item, edit a purchase and request CSV. The stock effect of purchase corrections and generated CSV contents were not verified.

### Workforce and payouts

Add a mobile-based user → assign a role at one or more shop locations → configure garment piece rates → assign garment or task work → review dues → select earning rows and record a payout → inspect payout history.

The live user form exposed name, mobile, optional email, shop locations, role and View Permissions. Existing mobile numbers are disabled in the edit path. Standard roles seen in the browser were Shop Manager, Office Staff, Worker, Senior Staff, Cutting Master, Tailor, Workshop Manager and Delivery Boy. They do not establish one fixed permission matrix for every shop.

Worker Dues can filter dates and paid state and group by worker or work date. Its payment action selects source earning rows, sums their returned rates, chooses a method and submits the selected IDs. Payouts is a separate dated report of recorded money. Assignment reports connect workers with their garment and task jobs. No wage calculation or payment was executed against live work.

## Permissions and store scope

The inspected code uses 14 business permission literals:

| Purpose | Symbols |
|---|---|
| Shop admission and administration | `WEB_ACCESS`, `ADMIN_CTRL`, `EDIT_SHOP` |
| Orders and work | `ADD_ORDER`, `EDIT_ORDER`, `ASSIGN_ITEM`, `MANAGE_TASK`, `VIEW_TASK` |
| Customers and gallery | `VIEW_CUST`, `VIEW_GALLERY`, `EDIT_GALLERY` |
| Financial information | `VIEW_PRICE`, `VIEW_REPORTS`, `MANAGE_PAYMENTS` |

The [permission reference](permission_symbols.csv) preserves their code locations. These are observed client symbols, not the complete server permission vocabulary. Built-in role rows hide edit/delete controls. Custom roles have their own name and selected permission IDs.

The application selects shops with `WEB_ACCESS`. Report filters add All location, while the header uses eligible shop records. A `-1` shop sentinel is treated specially by the permission helper and removed from outgoing shop filters. Backend checks on the resulting scope remain unverified.

Navigation, page guards, individual controls and server authorization are distinct. Only the signed-in account was exercised. The report-layout and some date/status click handlers do not repeat all of their related visibility checks.

## Settings and store setup

The two-step store wizard supports name, code, Outlet/Workshop/Both, Gents/Ladies/Both, main-shop flag, contact, email, website, Instagram, WhatsApp and Facebook. The second step includes location label, address, city, country, state, postal code, map position, logo and photo. Adding another shop can copy main-shop first-step values. The client disables another Workshop or Both choice after a non-Outlet store exists.

Settings exposes:

- Cms or Inch and offered services Stitching, Material and Readymade.
- Hide customer measurements, standard garment items and standard services.
- GST switch, GSTIN, percentage and include-GST-in-price choice.
- Random, Serial or Custom order numbering.
- Notification preferences for Received, In Progress, Completed, Ready For Trial, Delivered and Cancelled.
- Printed clauses, order-list period, invoice template and order-PDF template.

The browser confirmed four invoice formats: Standard, Consolidated and Price Breakup at A5, plus Tax Invoice India at A4. Five order-PDF formats were visible: Basic A5, Detailed A5, Minimal A5, Minimal A4 and Quick Print A5.

GST fields were opened in an unsaved preview. The switch returned to its saved state after navigating away. Notification preferences and document-format choices were inspected without testing an outgoing message or generated file.

## Reports, backup and subscriptions

Dashboard periods are Daily, Weekly, Monthly and Yearly, with location and date filtering. It shows sales, payments, material/readymade sales and order counts, plus charts based on returned API data. The prediction series is provided by the server; no client forecasting model was recovered.

| Report | Behavior |
|---|---|
| Insights | Ranks ordered items, customers, revenue dates and weekdays, with period and location filtering |
| Monthly | Payment, sales and order series by selected month/year |
| Sales | Groups returned sales by customer or order date and sums price |
| Payments | Groups receipts by customer or payment date and sums amount |
| Dues | Groups balances by customer or order date and totals dues |
| Bills | Lists bill/order identifiers and totals, then opens invoice documents |

Sales, Payments, Dues and Bills default to the preceding 90 days through today and request server-generated Excel with `rep_format: xls`. These are requests defined by the client, rather than verified spreadsheet files. In this empty shop, the corresponding views showed no data.

Backup data configures a schedule with an active flag, Daily/Weekly/Monthly/Yearly frequency, and delivery type. Its description refers to Excel email attachment or cloud upload with an emailed link. The actual first delivery choice is labeled `Daily`, and the second is `Upload to cloud`. That label mismatch was confirmed in an unsaved browser preview. This page does not establish an immediate backup download, restore workflow, history, or successful scheduled execution.

The live FAQ states a 30-day trial and four subscription plans. It gives no prices in that answer. The captured business routes and handlers did not establish a paid-plan matrix, feature entitlements, purchase or renewal flow. Those remain product claims and unknowns rather than recovered billing functionality.

## Data and integration references

The browser client uses a shared HTTP layer targeting `https://api.tailormateapp.com/v4`. The application is organized around users, shops, per-shop roles and permissions, customers, body and garment measurements, garment definitions, stitch types and features, orders and item lines, task definitions and instances, stock records, purchases, suppliers, receipts, discounts, expense heads and entries, worker earnings and payouts, galleries, settings and backup schedules.

The [API reference catalog](client_api_catalog.csv) contains 119 distinct literal method/path pairs. The [call-site index](client_api_calls.csv) retains all 285 occurrences, source offsets and literal parameter-object keys. Most repeated references are shared helpers bundled into several pages. These counts are not a complete API specification and do not establish successful requests.

Important service families include order list/detail/save/update, customer and measurement records, materials/readymades/purchases, workers and rates, permission roles, reports, uploads, printing and invoices. Dynamic paths and backend-only endpoints can be absent from the literal index.

Session credentials, request headers, cookies and OTP values were not collected. The login helper contains its own shipped Authorization literal; its value is omitted from authored outputs and was not used separately to call services. Its presence does not establish current validity or authorization scope.

## Material findings

These findings affect a reconstruction or requirements review. Except where a browser observation is named, they describe inspected client paths and remain untested with writes.

1. **Trial rows exceed the save fields.** The UI can append trial rows, but the payload only serializes three.
2. **Body-measurement copying can clear a value.** The order garment editor's empty-string test lets an undefined mapping pass, unlike the customer editor's numeric-value check.
3. **Customer measurement validation is not fully wired.** Schemas exist, but the captured customer body/garment save forms do not connect them through a resolver or explicit trigger. The order-specific editor does.
4. **Assignment-history status selections have no persistence path.** They update a local map that is absent from Assign submission.
5. **Task detail needs prior list cache.** The component can return nothing when the cached item is absent. Its lookup omits tomorrow-only rows, despite a task-detail request being available.
6. **Dues and Bills can share cache identity.** Their hooks both use `type: dues` for otherwise identical filter keys while requesting different endpoints. Explicit refetching means the visible effect depends on timing.
7. **Some request errors can reach success handlers.** Several helpers return an error-message string instead of throwing, while their callers accept anything without an explicit failure flag. Unit and size forms also test status truthiness rather than an exact success value.
8. **Some constraints remain on the server.** Payment positivity, overpayment, duplicate order numbers, stock-save atomicity and several numeric bounds are not established by the inspected client.
9. **Daily-expense date selection excludes today.** Its picker sets yesterday as the maximum selectable date, and editing disables date changes. That is a picker restriction, not proof that every other submission path rejects today's date.
10. **Some editing entry points differ from their icons.** Date/status containers can open mutation dialogs without repeating the icon's `EDIT_ORDER` condition. No lower-permission account or backend bypass was tested.
11. **Task-master drag support is uncertain.** A reorder callback exists, but its draggable flag starts false without a visible enabling action in that component. Garment measurement ordering uses a separate explicit path.
12. **Names can merge worker groups.** Dues grouping uses displayed names, and the Pay shortcut takes the first grouped worker ID. Duplicate-name behavior needs a real-data check.
13. **Backup delivery labeling is misleading.** Code 1 displays Daily as a delivery type. This was observed in the live form; actual delivery was not tested.

The [core findings](core_findings.md), [operations findings](operations_findings.md) and [platform findings](platform_findings.md) retain further details and source references. Their scope statements describe static subtasks. This report adds the parent investigation's browser evidence.

## Deliverables and validation

- [Complete catalog](feature_catalog.md), [CSV](feature_inventory.csv) and [JSON](feature_inventory.json).
- [Browser observations](browser_observations.csv) and [field index](browser_fields.csv).
- [Compiled page patterns](client_route_patterns.csv) and [captured HTML paths](captured_routes.csv).
- [HTTP catalog](client_api_catalog.csv), [call sites](client_api_calls.csv) and [permission symbols](permission_symbols.csv).
- [REA findings](rea_findings.md), [coverage summary](evidence/rea-summary.json), [source examination](evidence/rea-source-status.json) and [asset provenance](evidence/asset-provenance.json).
- [Validation result](validation.json) and [inventory totals](inventory_summary.json).

`python3 research_tailormate/build_inventory.py` regenerates the catalog and indexes, checks all 472 feature anchors, checks literal API offsets, and verifies all 213 captured-resource hashes. The REA summary separately verifies the identity of its 73 selected scripts and lossless compression of both Evidence bundles. These checks validate research artifacts rather than business writes.

`python3 research_tailormate/validate_artifacts.py` checks the final files, including CSV/JSON agreement, links, REA bundle digests, and the discarded settings previews.

core_findings.md.content:
# TailorMate core workflow findings

This source pass records 87 feature entries across 12 module groups, with 176 validated exact anchors into the captured shipped JavaScript. The inventory is [core_features.json](core_features.json). [build_core_features.py](build_core_features.py) regenerates it without executing the target application.

This pass used local captured assets and derived token-line reading views. It performed no browser interaction, network request, business write, upload, payment, message, or permission test. The parent investigation adds actual browser observations and REA Evidence IDs. Every entry remains code-defined.

## Feature groups

| Module group | Entries | Main behavior |
|---|---:|---|
| Customers | 8 | Customer register, search, details, photos, edit, deactivation, body and garment measurement history |
| Measurements | 8 | Gender templates, body measurements, garment profiles, inch-based values, reuse, copy, mapping, order snapshots |
| Order intake | 5 | Stitching, material and readymade categories, customer selection, category stepper and existing-order context |
| Stitching order entry | 12 | Garment names, stitch types, staff, visual options, charges, dates, trials, instructions, cloth and pattern images |
| Stock sale order entry | 5 | Material and readymade selection, stock limits, selling prices, line edits and shared order save |
| Order lists and search | 7 | Operational queues, periods, trials, loaded-row search, advanced filters and results |
| Order detail | 15 | Combined items, customer view, dates and numbers, status, editing, staff, cost and task actions, print and QR |
| Order payments and documents | 5 | New receipt, past receipts, discount records, form boundary, bills and payment advice |
| Garment costs and task planning | 5 | Expense heads, duplicate checks, profit preview, staff tasks, start-date estimate and plan locking |
| Tasks | 7 | Queue tabs, progress, start, finish, comments, reset and cache dependency |
| Work calendar | 4 | Four months, daily order drill-down, workload statistics and color ranges |
| Gallery | 6 | Folders, image uploads, favorites, deletion and carousel preview |

## Observed client model

The intake flow is category selection → customer selection → garment or stock selection → garment details for stitching → save → order detail. New orders, material sales, and readymade sales share `/saveneworder`. Existing orders use `/updateorder`. Adding an item reuses the wizard with customer, delivery date, and order ID in the URL.

Stitching defaults include quantity 1, a name composed from garment plus `#1`, default garment price, delivery time 17:00, no urgency, and an empty trial row. The garment detail stores measurements, selected stitch features, sales staff, per-item charges, due date and time, function date, trials, instructions, video link, cloth photos and pattern photos. Sales staff is capped at two. Garment and master measurement templates are server-provided. This pass did not invent fixed field sets from screenshots or template strings.

Material and readymade sales show stock, editable quantity and sell price. The client requires at least one positive quantity and rejects a selected quantity greater than displayed stock. Existing line quantities set to zero are submitted as inactive item updates. These are client validation and request-construction observations, not proof that stock updates succeed or share one backend transaction.

Order statuses are fetched from `/getorderstatus`. List queue names such as Active, Completed, and Delivered are filters, not proof of the complete stored status vocabulary. A task has explicit workflow values 1 Not Started, 2 In Progress, and 3 Completed. Task badge labels Completed, On Time, and Delayed are separate derived presentation values.

Order detail sums the garment price fields, material total prices, and readymade total prices, then subtracts receipts and discount. Discount is represented separately as `payment_type: "2"`, while receipts use type 1. Quantity expansion and any backend tax calculations are outside that summation. There is no basis to copy Tailorman's GST-percent calculation into this product.

The print helpers use `/printitem`, `/printorder`, and `/printqrcode`. Bill and payment-advice documents come from `/getorderinvoice`. WhatsApp controls open a composer with a document URL. They do not establish dispatch or delivery.

## Material source findings

### More trial rows can be entered than are serialized

The stitching form appends trial rows without a three-row limit. The request builder serializes only the first three as `trial_date`, `trial_date2`, and `trial_date3`. A fourth row can therefore exist in local UI state without a corresponding field in that save request. No order was submitted to test the result.

Source: [stitching handlers](evidence/assets/_next/static/chunks/9491-bcd4f8939976b832.js), anchors `children:"Add Trial"` and `trial_date3:` in the feature inventory.

### Copying body values behaves differently in the two garment editors

The customer-profile garment editor copies only nonzero numeric mapped values. The order garment editor checks the mapped value against an empty string. When no mapping exists, `undefined !== ""` is true, so it can replace an existing form value with undefined. The order-specific measurement validation can then report a required field. This is a static overwrite path, not an observed lost measurement.

Sources: [customer measurement form](evidence/assets/_next/static/chunks/3040-3fd2e3984ab95f57.js) and [order measurement form](evidence/assets/_next/static/chunks/9491-bcd4f8939976b832.js).

### Some declared measurement schemas are not wired into the customer editor

The customer-profile body and garment measurement sections declare schemas but instantiate their forms without a resolver or an explicit validation trigger in their save path. The order-specific garment measurement form does use its resolver and trigger. A reconstruction should preserve this distinction as current behavior and make any stricter validation an explicit new design decision.

Source: [customer form module](evidence/assets/_next/static/chunks/3040-3fd2e3984ab95f57.js), contrasted with the `resolver:(0,d.F)(eu)` path in the [stitching module](evidence/assets/_next/static/chunks/9491-bcd4f8939976b832.js).

### Assignment-history status controls have no persistence action

The Assign Staff modal presents history rows with an Update Status select. That select only writes to a local map. The Assign submission sends assigned staff, assigned piece rate and garment ID, and does not consume this history-status map. No separate save handler for those selections was found in the inspected module.

Source: [order detail](evidence/assets/_next/static/chunks/app/(apps)/orders/%5Btype%5D/%5BorderId%5D/page-b6d17c0c752aa831.js), `Work Assignment History` section.

### Task detail depends on a previous list cache

The task detail route fetches its tasks by garment ID, but it also retrieves the display row from the cached task-list response. If that cached row is unavailable, the component returns null. The cache helper combines active, completed, past-due, and today lists, but omits tomorrow-only tasks. Direct loading and tomorrow-only rows therefore need runtime checks with a real task.

Sources: [task detail](evidence/assets/_next/static/chunks/app/(apps)/tasks/%5BorderDressId%5D/page-a3f0226c050ee292.js), `if(!O)return null`, and [task cache helper](evidence/assets/_next/static/chunks/4486-d9bf3552840a4976.js).

### Some mutation entry points are less guarded than their icons

Order date and status containers open editing modals on click without the same `EDIT_ORDER` condition used for their pencil icons. Garment status is also directly clickable. The item action group and price blocks have their own permission conditions. This is an inconsistency in client control visibility, not proof of a backend permission bypass. No low-permission account was exercised.

Source: [order detail](evidence/assets/_next/static/chunks/app/(apps)/orders/%5Btype%5D/%5BorderId%5D/page-b6d17c0c752aa831.js).

### Payment amount constraints remain a backend question

The new-payment schema accepts a string amount and a date, with an optional payment method. The inspected edit and discount handlers forward amount strings without an explicit positive-number or balance limit. No invalid payment was submitted. The report should distinguish these client checks from unknown server validation.

Source: [order detail payment module](evidence/assets/_next/static/chunks/app/(apps)/orders/%5Btype%5D/%5BorderId%5D/page-b6d17c0c752aa831.js), `amount:ep.z.string(),date:ep.z.date()`.

### Task-plan and calendar validation are bounded

Task planning disables task choices, staff assignment, and day editing once a loaded task has started. Its save payload still serializes task status 1, so server preservation of progressed rows remains unverified. Calendar color settings validate nonempty range strings and at least one row, without numeric ordering or overlap validation in the captured schema.

Sources: [order task planner](evidence/assets/_next/static/chunks/app/(apps)/orders/%5Btype%5D/%5BorderId%5D/page-b6d17c0c752aa831.js) and [work calendar](evidence/assets/_next/static/chunks/app/(apps)/work-calendar/page-bb46a4fa83aa9a2f.js).

## Coverage boundary

The parent captured literal template HTML for order and task detail to discover their shipped chunks. That does not establish a valid order or garment record, successful detail load, or account access to another tenant. Dynamic data, status lists, measurement definitions, task templates, worker assignments, completed uploads, receipt balances, generated files and server validation remain runtime questions unless the parent supplies stronger evidence.

All feature source references resolve to the retained original script and exact character range. Reading views only add line breaks between tokens and were used for inspection. They are not original source, and they were not executed.

operations_findings.md.content:
# TailorMate operations feature findings

This static pass extracted 66 feature entries across 16 module groups from captured shipped TailorMate client JavaScript. The [operations feature JSON](operations_features.json) records each entry with exact original source text and a character offset. [build_operations_features.py](build_operations_features.py) regenerates the entries and checks every anchor.

The pass covers inventory, purchases, workers, worker reports, role administration, garment configuration, and expense administration. It did not use the browser, call APIs, submit business records, download reports, pay workers, or change settings. The parent investigation supplies browser observations and actual REA Evidence IDs. All entries remain code-defined.

## Inventory and purchases

Materials and readymades have separate stock records and API families. Both are scoped to the selected shop for their main list and save helpers. Material fields include name, type, unit, SKU, stock quantity, unit selling price, purchase unit price, supplier, and two image slots. Readymades replace material unit with one or more size selections and have their own type, purchase, and image IDs.

Both pages support case-insensitive search by name, type, or SKU. Lists show images, stock, price, and identifying information. Confirmed removal submits `is_active: "0"`. The code does not prove physical deletion. Current stock is directly editable in an item form. Purchase cost and supplier appear only on new-item forms, while later stock additions use a separate purchase dialog.

The shared Add Stock dialog requires quantity and purchase unit price and offers supplier selection. It selects the material or readymade purchase endpoint from the item type. Editing a purchase includes its original purchase ID. The date is restored or initialized to the current date, then displayed as text rather than offered as an editable date field.

The Purchases report defaults to 180 days and filters materials, readymades, or both. SKU filtering is debounced by 500 ms. Users can group by date or item name, inspect quantity and unit price, open a purchase for editing, and request a server-generated CSV. Actual stock mutation, purchase corrections, and CSV contents were not exercised.

Reference masters separately manage material types, material units and codes, readymade types, and readymade sizes and codes. Type/name minimums vary: material types, material units, and sizes require two characters, while readymade types require three. Item stock and price schemas use nonempty strings, not explicit positive-number bounds.

Sources include [materials](evidence/assets/_next/static/chunks/app/(apps)/inventory/materials/page-7140a18374176234.js), [readymades](evidence/assets/_next/static/chunks/app/(apps)/inventory/readymades/page-01a303d34371e3c1.js), [purchase report](evidence/assets/_next/static/chunks/app/(apps)/inventory/purchases/page-7caaf1783110a7f4.js), and [shared stock and purchase handlers](evidence/assets/_next/static/chunks/2869-5bf5afa4deeb80bb.js).

## Workers and permission roles

The worker directory shows full name, role, dial code, and mobile. User creation and editing have name, optional email, role, and a multi-select of shop locations. Save maps each location to a role in `shop_roles`. Existing mobile numbers are disabled, with guidance to remove and recreate a user to change one. This uses mobile identity rather than the email/password staff-creation pattern found in Tailorman.

View Permissions opens a role selector and a disabled list of permission choices. Roles and Permissions is a separate editable master. It fetches permission IDs and descriptions, saves selected IDs as `permission_id` objects, and permits custom role creation, editing, and deactivation. Built-in rows with `user_id` equal to `0` have no edit or delete actions. Those are client rules, with no tested backend authorization claim.

Worker rows show the dress-piece-rate action when `can_assign_order` is `"1"`. The rate editor loads garment definitions and current worker rates and saves one rate per dress. Existing rates cleared to blank or zero are submitted with `status_id: "1"`. New blank or zero rates are omitted. The server meaning of that status was not independently established.

Sources: [worker directory and rate editor](evidence/assets/_next/static/chunks/app/(apps)/workers/worker-list/page-b8f30e109a1a06cf.js), [roles editor](evidence/assets/_next/static/chunks/app/(apps)/workers/roles-and-permissions/page-ff9ab0dbf4d64dbd.js), and [role APIs](evidence/assets/_next/static/chunks/7970-0d13abf020d20796.js).

## Worker dues, payouts, and assignment reports

Worker Dues defaults to 180 days, can filter Paid, Unpaid, or both, and groups by worker name or work date. Its URL stores the selected dates, paid status, and grouping. Rows distinguish Dress and Task earnings and open the corresponding order. The source of the displayed rate is the returned worker-payment report. This pass does not infer a wage formula beyond summing those rates.

Pay Workers loads unpaid rows for one worker and initially selects all returned earning IDs. Users can select individual rows, select all, review the summed total, choose a payment method, and mark the selected rows paid. The request includes a total, payment mode, target worker ID, and an array of source IDs with Dress/Task type and paid state. No payment was submitted.

Payouts is a separate report of money already recorded. It filters dates and optional worker and groups by worker name or payment date, with per-group totals and payment-method labels. Both reports support server-generated CSV exports. No payout-edit or void control was found in the inspected payout component, which is a bounded observation about this page.

Task Assignments lists worker, role, task name, and job count. Dress Assignments groups jobs by worker. Each can open a list of assigned items with thumbnail, garment name, order number, store location, and due date. Selecting an item loads order/garment detail. The nested detail receives a `VIEW_PRICE` permission flag. The core inventory covers the actual item-level assignment and task lifecycle controls, so they are not duplicated here.

Sources: [dues](evidence/assets/_next/static/chunks/app/(apps)/workers/worker-dues/page-9bc4685a002c8f5b.js), [payouts](evidence/assets/_next/static/chunks/app/(apps)/workers/worker-payouts/page-7b4bab8819be29f0.js), and [shared assignment detail and report APIs](evidence/assets/_next/static/chunks/1702-93fae2de0ab3bd23.js).

## Administration masters

Task definitions have name, days required, and stored order. Custom garment definitions have name, gender, and optional default price. Each garment can have its own measurement configuration and stitching-feature groups.

Adding garment measurements has two steps: select gender-specific icons, then provide names for new selections. Existing selections are disabled and excluded from new-entry payloads. Measurement editing can change the name and icon. The measurement list supports deletion and immediate drag-order saves. Stitching groups have selectable rows, image-option previews, drag ordering, and an explicit Save Stitching action that marks selected groups active and unselected groups inactive.

User settings can hide standard garment items or standard stitch-type services. Standard stitch-type and bill-term rows owned by user `0` hide edit/delete actions. Bill terms store description text. Price add-ons store a name and a fixed price string for later order charges. These masters are separate from an actual garment order and its selected measurements, stitching options, and charges.

Expense Heads defines reusable names and scope: Shop Level, Item Level, or Shop & Item Level. Daily Shop Expenses records actual amount and date under a selected head. The daily list is filtered by current shop and supports name search, edit, and soft removal.

Sources include [task definitions](evidence/assets/_next/static/chunks/app/(apps)/admin/tasks/page-b00259c84aed8d14.js), [garment definitions and configuration](evidence/assets/_next/static/chunks/app/(apps)/admin/dresses/page-e19875bcaf38fb21.js), [expense heads](evidence/assets/_next/static/chunks/app/(apps)/admin/expenses/page-4141e559a0672a08.js), and [daily expenses](evidence/assets/_next/static/chunks/app/(apps)/shop-expenses/page-2dd9d2c8b34c6803.js).

## Material findings and remaining limits

1. Several API helpers catch exceptions and return `e.message` instead of throwing. For example, the material helper returns an error string, while the material form treats any result without an explicit `status` or `type` of `"fail"` as success. A caught request error can therefore take the success branch in the inspected client. This was not tested with a submitted save.
2. Material-unit and readymade-size forms test only whether the returned `status` is truthy. A nonempty status value such as `"fail"` would satisfy that client condition. The actual API response contract is not available.
3. Daily expense creation configures `maxDate` as yesterday, and edit mode disables date changes. The normal picker therefore excludes today and future dates in this inspected code. The amount schema is a plain string without a positive-number bound. Browser and server enforcement may add constraints not established by this pass.
4. The task master contains a reorder callback and passes a draggable state into the table, but that state starts false and no enabling control was found in this component. A reorder callback alone does not establish a usable task-drag workflow. The garment-measurement and stitching-feature lists explicitly set draggable true and use different paths.
5. Worker report grouping uses displayed names rather than stable IDs. If two workers share a name, their rows can appear in one group. The Pay shortcut then takes the first row's worker ID. Actual duplicate-name data was not available to test that case.
6. Purchase mutations and their CSV exports were not run. The shared purchase modal displays a date but does not expose an editor for it. Server-side stock adjustments when editing a purchase, rejection of negative values, and supplier persistence remain unverified.
7. The generic delete confirmation says that the account will be permanently deleted even when a row action merely sends `is_active: "0"` for a material, worker, role, or master. That shared wording is not evidence of account deletion.

The report makes no claim that every client permission is enforced by the backend, that a success banner proves a successful write, or that the visible reports contain every server record. The parent report should preserve those distinctions when combining this pass with browser observations.

## Validation

`python3 research_tailormate/build_operations_features.py` validates all 132 anchors against the exact original source and writes 66 entries. Offsets use Python string character positions in the retained decoded source. The token-line reading views were used for navigation only and are not the cited evidence. No missing dependency or page blocked this operations inventory.

platform_findings.md.content:
# TailorMate platform and reporting findings

This static pass produced 56 code-defined entries across eight module groups in [platform_features.json](platform_features.json). It inspected captured, shipped JavaScript and traced the page handlers into their shared request helpers. All 164 evidence anchors and character offsets pass [build_platform_features.py](build_platform_features.py).

The parent investigation supplies browser observations and actual REA Evidence IDs separately. This subtask did not use the browser, contact the application network, send an OTP, create an account, change settings, submit a store, configure a backup, download a report, or send a message. Source offsets refer to Python Unicode string positions in the retained original files, not the inserted lines in derived reading views.

## Identity and shop admission

Sign-in uses mobile number and country dial code. The form defaults to India and submits a Web device marker, a fixed device identifier, and user type 1. The `/login` response supplies a user ID for a four-digit OTP form. The OTP panel says the code was sent to email and WhatsApp. That wording does not establish either delivery channel's success.

OTP validation is automatic when all four numeric boxes have a value. The inputs advance focus and support Backspace and horizontal arrows. The visible Validate button has no separate click handler in the inspected component. An invalid response clears the inputs. Success stores the returned token and user in localStorage and updates auth context. Registration has identity and consent, phone, then OTP steps. Name requires three characters, email must be valid, and consent to the two linked policy documents is required.

The application reads `user_permissions` by user ID, selects a shop containing `WEB_ACCESS`, and redirects a user without a shop ID to first-store setup. The first-store page reuses the store wizard and updates the local user with the returned shop ID. When a nonempty permission response has no eligible web-access shop, the client clears local auth and queries and returns to sign-in.

The common HTTP client targets `https://api.tailormateapp.com/v4`. It adds the stored session Bearer header when a caller has not provided its own Authorization. The login/signup/OTP helper supplies a shipped Authorization literal of its own. Its value is deliberately omitted from authored findings. The source alone does not establish the literal's current validity or server permissions.

Sources are the captured [login page](evidence/assets/_next/static/chunks/app/auth/login/page-d1f0bd00b22e23fb.js), [registration page](evidence/assets/_next/static/chunks/app/auth/register/page-32052fee7386c7b3.js), [application layout](evidence/assets/_next/static/chunks/app/(apps)/layout-7a41b882bc0f5805.js), [first-store page](evidence/assets/_next/static/chunks/app/create-shop/page-25f8c06f2c1a8147.js), and [API client](evidence/assets/_next/static/chunks/5075-dc3f169160ed7450.js).

## Permissions describe actions and shops

This part of the client uses granular permission strings rather than a fixed universal list of admin, cashier, or tailor roles. It checks `VIEW_REPORTS`, `MANAGE_PAYMENTS`, `ADD_ORDER`, `VIEW_CUST`, `VIEW_GALLERY`, `VIEW_TASK`, `ADMIN_CTRL`, `EDIT_SHOP`, and `WEB_ACCESS` in the inspected paths.

Metrics navigation requires both reports and payment permission. The dashboard itself checks `VIEW_REPORTS` and redirects a denied user to active orders. Payment totals have a separate display gate. Store add/edit/remove controls check `EDIT_SHOP`. The report-section layout renders its tabs without repeating those sidebar checks, so menu hiding must not be described as proven server authorization.

Report location selectors explicitly include All location plus the loaded stores. The header instead derives options from `WEB_ACCESS` records. It recognizes a `-1` All locations sentinel when selected, but does not itself append an All locations option based on the number of stores. The shared permission helper treats that sentinel as allowed, and the API interceptor removes the sentinel `shop_id` from request arguments. Backend scope checks remain unknown.

The actual header includes Light and Dark choices, a desktop fullscreen action, and mobile menu controls. Generic source widgets for storage usage, Premium upgrade, chat, e-commerce, and template UI routes should not be counted as TailorMate business functionality without a reachable handler or browser evidence. The captured active navigation and page handlers do not establish a subscription-price matrix, renewal workflow, billing gateway, or feature entitlements by paid plan.

Source: [navigation and permission helpers](evidence/assets/_next/static/chunks/1892-b3ffd2b6cbf9e410.js).

## Store management

The store directory lists logo, name, location, main-store indicator, Outlet/Workshop badges, email, contact, and join date. Search filters loaded shop names. Store removal submits `status_id: -1` to the same save endpoint. The confirmation dialog's generic account-deletion wording is broader than the actual shop mutation.

The wizard has two steps. Basic details contain name, code, Outlet/Workshop/Both, Gents/Ladies/Both, main-shop flag, contact, email, website and social/contact IDs. Address details contain location label, address, city, country, state, postal code, map selection, logo and photo. Country changes fetch states and clear the previous state. Map search geocodes a chosen place and previews a marker before selecting latitude and longitude.

Adding another store can copy the main store's first-step details. The inspected copy handler does not copy the address step. The existing non-Outlet store check disables Workshop and Both choices with "Only one workshop is allowed". That is a client constraint, not a verified concurrent or server-side limit.

Sources: [store directory](evidence/assets/_next/static/chunks/app/(apps)/stores/page-b6432f9699257d78.js) and [shared store wizard](evidence/assets/_next/static/chunks/9371-4f67be6f8c235cf7.js).

## Settings

Settings save the following user-level choices:

- Measurement unit CMS or IN, displayed as Cms or Inch.
- Offered services Stitching, Material, and Readymade, with at least one selected.
- Hide measurements from the customer, hide standard dress items, and hide standard services.
- GST bill, GSTIN, percentage, and inclusive-price choice.
- Random, Serial, or Custom order-number pattern.
- Customer-notification order-status choices.
- Printed bill clauses about advance, returns, and color guarantee.
- Order-list window of 1-10 days or selected longer periods through one year.
- Invoice and order-PDF document-template IDs, shown with thumbnails and names.

The save handler encodes flags as `1` or `0` and selected lists as comma-separated IDs. Turning GST off clears the GST detail values in the payload. The page schema does not validate GSTIN format or bound the percentage. Actual order calculations belong to the order handlers and were outside this subtask.

Notification preferences do not themselves send a customer message. Document-template selection does not prove every output has been rendered or that the hide-measurement choice is enforced in every channel.

Source: [settings page](evidence/assets/_next/static/chunks/app/(apps)/settings/page-8e56f7911d5a369e.js).

## Backup is a schedule

The Backup data page reads and saves a per-user schedule with active flag, frequency, and delivery type. Frequencies are Daily, Weekly, Monthly, and Yearly. Disabling clears frequency and delivery type in the next submitted payload.

The description says backups can be sent as an Excel email attachment or uploaded to the cloud with an emailed link. The two actual delivery labels are `Daily` for code 1 and `Upload to cloud` for code 2. The first label appears to be a delivery-choice defect. The backend interpretation is not recoverable from that label alone.

No immediate export, restore, backup-history list, delivery history, or file-generation handler appears in this captured page module. That is a page-scoped negative finding, not proof that the server or mobile app lacks those capabilities.

Source: [backup schedule page](evidence/assets/_next/static/chunks/app/(apps)/backup-data/page-77033a376f45b7ad.js).

## Dashboard and reports

The dashboard switches among daily, weekly, monthly, and yearly periods. It selects a location, normalizes the start date, and calls the dashboard report endpoint. Counters include sales, payments, material sales, readymade sales, orders received, delivered, past due, and upcoming. The upcoming label reads the API field `orders_due_today`.

Dashboard charts display API-provided monthly order counts, sales-type values, and current versus predicted sales. The client does not implement a forecasting model. The order chart appends the browser's current month abbreviation to returned day values, even for another selected period. A historical populated chart should be checked before reconstructing that behavior.

The six report sections are Insights, Monthly, Sales, Payments, Dues, and Bills:

- Insights defaults to yearly and ranks ordering items, customers by order value, revenue dates, and weekday performance from server results.
- Monthly displays payments, sales, and orders as month/year bar series.
- Sales groups `all_sales` by customer or order date and sums `price` per group.
- Payments groups `all_payments` by customer or payment date and sums `amount` per group.
- Dues groups `all_dues` by customer or order date, showing original amount and remaining dues and summing dues per group.
- Bills lists bill number, order number, date, and total, then opens an invoice preview with download/print and a prefilled WhatsApp composer.

The last four default to the preceding 90 days through today. They support location and date filtering and request server-generated Excel with `rep_format: xls`. Grouping is client-side, but the original report records and their period semantics come from the server. A code path calling a download helper is not a verified spreadsheet, and a WhatsApp composer is not a sent message.

One shared-key issue needs a runtime check. The Dues hook and Bills hook both construct their React Query key with `type: "dues"` and otherwise the same filter/user fields, while calling different endpoints. Those views can share cached response identity for matching dates and shop. Both pages also explicitly refetch when their arguments change, so the exact visible failure depends on query timing. Do not declare either report broken from this static evidence alone.

Sources: [dashboard](evidence/assets/_next/static/chunks/app/(apps)/page-dc9b232cad4b57dc.js), [report hooks and endpoints](evidence/assets/_next/static/chunks/2280-431fea3a652d0870.js), [shared filters](evidence/assets/_next/static/chunks/8852-96ea6dc9aa39cc2a.js), and the report-page sources named in each feature entry.

## Support and runtime limits

FAQs are remote question/answer values in a single-open accordion. Contact us supplies WhatsApp, email, and website links. It does not have an in-app support-ticket form in the inspected component.

The auth provider waits for browser mount, optional country loading, and Google Maps Places loading before rendering children. Startup dependency or Maps failure behavior should be tested separately. Local auth state, request construction, API error handling, and query invalidation are client evidence. They do not establish backend access control, OTP delivery, data isolation, successful writes, scheduled execution, or offline capability.

All feature entries keep those limits explicit. The parent report can attach authenticated screen evidence without promoting every code-defined action to a tested result.

rea_findings.md.content:
# REA findings and coverage

The installed [reverse-engineer-anything skill](/Users/nishanth/.agents/skills/reverse-engineer-anything/SKILL.md) guided the investigation. The existing `rea-agents` 6.8.0 CLI supplied the documented JavaScript fallback because no REA MCP tool was connected. No installation, application bootstrap execution, or separate browser launch was needed.

The shared T3 browser supplied navigation and response-text acquisition. Read-only source work was split into orders/customer/workshop, operations, and platform/reporting scopes, as the REA skill directs for independent questions. The parent investigation validated the returned artifacts and browser evidence.

## Acquired artifact

The capture contains 213 resources: 163 JavaScript files and 50 HTML responses. Sources were discovered from rendered resources, script references, navigation definitions, and linked route patterns. The exact decoded response text was serialized and written to local UTF-8 files. Browser-computed SHA-256 values match the retained bytes. These are decoded-text identities, not compressed wire-byte or publisher-signature claims.

The [provenance index](evidence/asset-provenance.json) records URL, status, file, byte count and digest. [unpack_evidence.py](unpack_evidence.py) reproduces the extraction from acquisition JSON and checks hashes.

Literal `/orders/active/[id]` and `/tasks/[id]` requests were used only to discover dynamic page chunks. They did not contain valid record IDs, and their client detail handlers were not executed to retrieve such records. The gallery was also inspected through an existing standard folder in the authenticated browser.

## Static reading views

[index_sources.mjs](index_sources.mjs) uses the installed Babel parser on all 163 captured scripts. It builds an inert index of 2,434 webpack module occurrences, their dependencies and string literals. It also creates reading views by inserting line breaks between tokens. Target code is never imported or executed by this script.

Reading views are derived inspection aids rather than original source. Catalog citations use the original retained scripts. Character offsets in the catalog use zero-based Unicode code points, and the consolidated JSON also records UTF-8 byte offsets and UTF-16 offsets. AST-derived indexes label their UTF-16 locations separately.

The API index selects literal string arguments to `.get`, `.post`, `.put`, `.patch` and `.delete`. It retains 285 call sites and 119 distinct method/path pairs. It is a client-reference inventory, not an OpenAPI schema, endpoint availability test, or complete server-route list. Generic toast action strings were excluded from the authored business-permission index.

## Main REA run

Parent Evidence ID: `ev_bf09d26d9c77a4857ed9b8a406e4558fc92086a8f94525167deb447617d4b7f4`.

The target tree initially contained 156 captured scripts. An explicit selection examined 67 application-page, layout and business-helper scripts. All 67 completed syntax parsing and examination, with zero parse failures. The other 89 were outside this run's source selection. The run read 1,443,625 text bytes and visited 394,334 AST nodes.

The application and semantic graphs are partial. The semantic graph is truncated and reports 31,804 retained unknowns. Reported constraints include configured semantic ceilings, parent-result admission, semantic-result budget, worker heap and worker deadline budgets. Completion of source examination does not resolve those graph limitations.

The selected command used the existing launcher and these arguments:

```text
rea analyze-javascript-application <absolute evidence/assets directory>
  --source-paths-json <absolute evidence/rea-source-selection.json>
  --max-semantic-nodes 60000 --max-semantic-nodes-per-file 5000
  --max-semantic-unknowns 60000 --max-semantic-unknowns-per-file 5000
  --detail summary --evidence_output <absolute evidence/rea-evidence.json> --json
```

## Supplementary run

Parent Evidence ID: `ev_645eb6bfdb71406c56af20b9bdce7d99d3cd01a77a2adcc1f4e6c336d443fac5`.

Later discovery added seven scripts, including one loading component. The supplementary selection examined the six functional additions: gallery images, order detail, advanced order search, task detail, and first-store page and layout. It did not repeat the main selection.

All six completed syntax parsing and examination with zero parse failures. The run read 194,978 text bytes and visited 52,289 AST nodes. Its semantic graph is also partial. It used the same per-file semantic ceilings and total ceilings of 30,000 instead of 60,000. The source selection is retained in [rea-supplement-selection.json](evidence/rea-supplement-selection.json).

The two artifact-root digests differ because the directory grew from 156 to 163 scripts between runs. The [source status file](evidence/rea-source-status.json) ties each examined source to its Evidence ID and retained digest.

## Combined coverage and retained Evidence

REA examined 73 unique selected application scripts from 163 captured scripts. All 73 have complete syntax status and matching current source hashes. Ninety captured scripts were not selected. These include loading, framework, vendor and supporting UI code. This selected scope does not establish complete application semantics or backend recovery.

The overall per-file `parse_status` is partial for all 73 because it includes unresolved semantic findings. The syntax-specific coverage field is complete for those files. The machine summary keeps these two measures separate.

Both CLI runs returned successfully. No TailorMate provider timeout required a retry. Explicit graph truncation and unknowns remain recorded rather than treated as absent functionality.

Retained files include:

- [Main summary output](evidence/rea-summary-output.json) and [supplementary summary output](evidence/rea-supplement-summary-output.json).
- [Combined coverage and digests](evidence/rea-summary.json) and [source status](evidence/rea-source-status.json).
- [Full main Evidence, gzip](evidence/rea-evidence.json.gz) and [full supplementary Evidence, gzip](evidence/rea-supplement-evidence.json.gz).
- [Source selection](evidence/rea-source-selection.json) and [supplementary selection](evidence/rea-supplement-selection.json).

The complete bundles were compressed losslessly. Each decompressed digest was verified against its original JSON before the duplicate uncompressed output was removed. [summarize_rea.py](summarize_rea.py) reproduces the source checks and compression verification.

## Finding ledger

| Question | Evidence | Result and limit |
|---|---|---|
| Which functions exist in the web client? | Captured pages/helpers, both REA parents, exact source anchors | 209 entries. Static control paths do not prove successful writes. |
| Which business areas are reachable here? | 71 authenticated states and two public states | Main navigation, empty lists, seeded masters, safe forms and previews inspected. No worker impersonation or other-shop testing. |
| How do order, measurement and task flows work? | Garment editors, order detail, measurement helpers, task module | Client fields and payloads recovered. Populated detail, numeric server rules and stock atomicity remain untested. |
| Are prices and subscriptions recovered? | Live FAQ, navigation, page code | FAQ claims 30-day trial and four plans. No verified price/entitlement matrix or renewal flow. |
| Is backup working? | Schedule handler and unsaved browser preview | Schedule fields confirmed, including delivery label mismatch. No schedule was saved and no file or delivery was observed. |
| What remains unknown? | Partial graphs, source-selection boundaries, empty account | Backend schema/rules, dynamic server values, completed outputs, scheduled jobs, payment side effects and mobile-only capabilities. |

The [main report](tailormate_feature_report.md) combines browser and static findings while retaining those limits.

feature_entries.details: Dashboard requests location-aware summary data; renders revenue, orders, customers, overdue work, and recent activity.
feature_entries.verification_gap: Browser visibility and successful server persistence are separate checks.
feature_entries.browser_scope: Related screen or form inspected; this does not verify every capability in this entry.

feature_entries.details: Client requests payment summary for optional start date, end date, and location.
feature_entries.verification_gap: Browser visibility and successful server persistence are separate checks.
feature_entries.browser_scope: Related screen or form inspected; this does not verify every capability in this entry.

feature_entries.details: Links to customer creation, tailoring order entry, boutique sale, and payment recording adapt to business type.
